static_checks: 0 drift failures, 0 audit errors, 0 glossary problems
visual_review: every tour screenshot compared with the English build and with the previous build, by reviewers looking for clipping, overlap, mirroring, digit order, glyphs, English left and visible translation errors; every finding checked by a second reviewer who tried to refute it. Four further rounds made saves and tours for screens no earlier test reached (the Hall of Fame and credits, the challenge menus, Kurt and the move relearner, PokéGear calls, Rare Candy and TM use, the battle debug menu, the Safari Zone, the Berry Blender, Pokéblocks, Voltorb Flip, map-name pop-ups, marts, the gym badge scenes, the Battle Frontier facilities, the Trainer Hill and Battle Tents, PC storage, Pokédex forms, help windows, Easy Chat, contests, a double battle, the Battle Arena and the Dome tourney tree, the Frontier Pass map and results, the Pyramid Bag, berry tags, the clock reset, the Places & People radio show, the debug menu and nicknames of ten wide letters); a fifth round reached the Battle Factory from rental to swap, a contest in every category from entry to ribbon, the Pokédex form pages, field moves, the legendary and totem encounters, and the NPCs whose lines still showed English names; a sixth round reached the gym leader and Elite Four rematches, the remaining in-game trades, the NPC service menus, player and box names typed in Hebrew, every summary and move-relearner text, the post-game Alola and Sinjoh encounters, the route, dungeon and gym trainers, the Johto and Kanto story scenes and battles, item pickups and gifts, gift Pokémon and eggs, the Frontier lounge and Scott, named gift Pokémon and their mail, and the post-game legends; a seventh round reached every Battle Dome and Battle Tower trainer's card, tree slot and intro, and the Trainer Hill's Variety, Unique and Expert floors, and gave every item that can be held in a count its Hebrew plural, shown on screen with the longest names and the widest counts in the bag, the PC, the Pyramid bag and the marts; an eighth round reached the bag's sort in every pocket, tossing to the end, status cures in and out of battle, a Repel or Lure used while one is active, field items used in the wrong place, and the thirteen dojo invitations; a ninth round reached every contest opponent and the COOL Normal and Master contests from entry to ribbon; a tenth round played through the post-game League road with the Elite Four rematch and every island a player reaches after it, and every town, route, bridge and gate, reading each sign, talking to each person and entering each building; the same round opened every shop's full buy and sell lists, every item in every bag pocket with its description, and checked every name that is not a Pokémon's against the glossary; an eleventh round reached every gym leader, guide and statue after the badge, the leaders' dojo rematch offers, the PC mailbox with every mail design, all 90 Battle Tent trainers and a trainer withdrawing a Pokémon; a twelfth round played the Battle Dome and Battle Palace double challenges and the Tower double, multi and Factory double formats; a thirteenth round forced men, women and pairs to withdraw a Pokémon in single, double and multi battles, opened every Frontier results window with multi-digit records, typed nicknames with quote marks in all three summary fonts, showed EXEGGUTOR-A in every window that names it, and drew the trade screen, link battles, the cable club and record-mixing lines and the Mystery Gift menus with the link partner faked in memory; a fourteenth round built a diagnostic ROM that records every translated string as it is copied or printed, listed the ones no tour had shown, and drew the reachable rest in their real windows: every battle message with the longest names, the battle debug menu, contest effects, paintings and the Berry Blender, the radio and the PokéGear CONDITION screens, the Frontier Brain and Trainer Hill intros, the Day Care, the PC mailbox, every item plural and Pokédex category, and the link records and VS screen; a sixteenth round showed the Pokédex entry, evolution page and species name of every Pokémon that only the randomizer brings into the game, in the Pokédex, party, summary, PC and battle windows, and played a randomized new game to its first catches; a last round gave Hebrew names to the words that dialogue and Pokédex entries still printed in Latin, such as POKéRUS, Mr. Fuji, Daisy, Hisui and the Ultra Wormhole, and showed every changed line in its window, the Pokédex entries also on their caught pages and on the radio's Pokédex Show; the confirmed misalignments are fixed and seen on screen before and after
crosscore_notes: All six cores load the save and draw every screen like mGBA. What is left: the title frame differs on every core because the intro animation runs at a different point when the save loads; on the main menu, the two buttons the game darkens with the GBA's brightness effect come out one step of the GBA's 5-bit colour apart; the start menu shows the time, and each core's clock started at a different second; and the bag's pocket arrows (VBA-M, VBA-Next, SkyEmu) and Mednafen-GBA's party icons are caught on another frame of their animation.

map_walk.held_reason: because the map starts a scripted Frontier or multi-battle sequence that the walker (which answers every prompt with B) cannot finish
map_walk.hebrew_only_reason: hold because the first Battle Arena battle was won in this run and the walker stopped at the next-opponent menu, which is drawn correctly; in the English run that battle ended back in the lobby

known_issues_intro: The decisions behind the translation are in `translation/hebrew/DECISIONS.md` of the source fork.
known_issues: Ariana's class name מנהל רוקט is masculine because she shares the class with Archer, Proton and Petrel; other classes shared by men and women also keep the noun the trainer data gives them (DECISIONS.md Q124, Q127).
not_tested: Real hardware. No flashcart was available. The ROM is 32 MiB and needs a cart that supports 32 MiB images, with the save type set to FLASH 128 KB and a working RTC.
Playing by hand in a GUI. Every run above was automated. The tours type a Hebrew name and walk through menus and battles, but nobody played from a new game to the first badge.
A real 2.0.x save from a long playthrough. The save ladder was built with the harness and the debug menu.

A real link with a second GBA. The trade screen, link battles, the cable club and record-mixing lines and the Mystery Gift menus were seen on screen with the partner faked in memory. The Union Room and the wireless group screens need a Wireless Adapter and were not seen; their strings passed the width audit only.

C strings no tour shows. A diagnostic build lists every translated C string the tours put on screen. The Pokédex entries and species names of Pokémon that only the randomizer brings into the game were shown on Pokédex pages filled in memory, which match the real caught pages pixel for pixel; a randomized new game was played to its first catches, but not every species was rolled. Not shown are 7 evolution-method words that the Pokédex evolution page never prints in H&S, about 35 lines that need a state the tours could not set up, and about 2,300 that H&S 2.0.6 cannot reach (link and wireless screens, switched-off features, Emerald and FireRed leftovers, unused data). Their widths were checked by the layout audit and by reviewers against the code, not on screen.
Female address. The player is addressed in the masculine throughout (a decision of this translation).
The randomizer and challenge options beyond their menus.

Easy Chat in full. The words and the ABC keyboard are Hebrew. Seen on screen: the four Day Care hint windows; the Odd Egg interview with its group keyboard, every key of the Hebrew ABC keyboard and every one of its 23 letter lists, the status, voices, feelings and actions lists and the YES/NO prompts; Pichu's password giving the egg; the Battle Tower feelings man's start, win and loss screens; the contest and Battle Tower interviews, the apprentice's win speech and the mart questionnaire, opened with their script; writing mail from the bag; and the first Trainer Hill floor's trainer lines. Not seen: the Battle Frontier facility trainers' lines, the other ten Odd Egg passwords, and phrases that come from a linked game.
Cores other than the six listed, and RetroArch builds for Android or handhelds.

Most of the 525 item plural names. The bag, PC, Pyramid and mart count lines were seen on screen with a sample of them, the longest names and the widest counts; the rest were checked against the glossary rules and by tools/hebrew/plurals.py, which fails when a stackable item has no plural.

Names of Pokémon from Gen 4 on, and many trainer names, are transliterations marked "proposed" in the glossary. All 1,851 were reviewed against the transliteration rules, the official English pronunciation and consistency with related names, and 22 of the 23 changes it proposed were made (`translation/hebrew/DECISIONS.md`), but none was checked against an official Hebrew source or by a native speaker on screen.
